question: *** ROW 129. What became of ISABELLA BRAILEY *** , born London (St Andrew) about 1841, daughter of John Brailey and Georgina Temple? *** Last seen aged 20, unmarried, a NEEDLE WOMAN, in her widowed mother's house at Lower Gunstone, Bideford, in 1861. ***
searches run: *** Marriages, BRAILEY and BRAYLEY, Devon 1861-1890: none. *** *** Marriages, both spellings, ALL of England and Wales 1858-1895: none. *** *** Deaths, both spellings, all England and Wales 1861-1925: none. ***
answer: *** SHE VANISHES FROM THE ENGLISH CIVIL REGISTERS AFTER 1861, AND THE NULL IS CONTROLLED. *** The control: *** BRAYLEY marriages with no forename, 1870 alone, returns FOURTEEN nationally *** - so the surname is thickly indexed and the searches were capable of finding her. *** She did not marry in England and she did not die in England under either spelling. *** The readings that fit: she EMIGRATED; or she married or died under one of the manglings this surname is notorious for. *** Nothing here decides between them. ***

question: *** ROW 130. Is GEORGINA BRAYLEY, born London Kilburn about 1871 *** - a general servant in a draper's house at Tower Street, Northam, in 1891 - *** a daughter of JOHN WALKER BRAYLEY? ***
searches run: *** Marriages, BRAYLEY, forename "John Walker", 1863-1880, all counties. ***
answer: *** REFUTED, and cleanly. *** *** JOHN WALKER BRAYLEY MARRIED IN THE DECEMBER QUARTER OF 1876, AT BIDEFORD - 5b/978. *** That is *** FIVE YEARS AFTER *** a child born at Kilburn in 1871. *** She cannot be his daughter by that marriage ***, and the pattern this archive was reasoning from - a Brayley of the right age, in service at Northam, carrying the family's forename - *** was a resemblance and nothing more. She is not adopted. ***
